problem_statement: A caller cannot dedicate a reserved portion of the shared heap to a specific subsystem. There is no way to create a named region with a fixed allocation limit: the heap allocator offers no interface to register such a region, so a request to do so cannot be honored. The expected behavior, as exercised by the upstream test, is that attempting to register a region with a NULL name, with a zero size, or with a name that duplicates an already-registered region is reported as an invalid registration; a valid registration returns a usable region identifier distinct from the general pool; an allocation requested within that region up to its reserved size succeeds and is freeable; an allocation requested within the region that exceeds its reserved size is refused (returns NULL) even though the overall heap still has free space; and a same-sized allocation drawn from the general pool succeeds independently of the dedicated region being exhausted.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: HeapMem must support registering a dedicated logical zone of the heap (with a reserved size limit) so a subsystem can get prioritized memory; allocations are tagged to a zone and refused when they would exceed the zone's reserved limit, while a GENERAL zone preserves the prior behavior.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "allocations are tagged to a zone". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally

causal_chain: The upstream zones test exercises a heap allocator that can reserve a named, dedicated region of the shared heap with a fixed allocation limit. Before the production fix the allocator exposes no interface to register such a region and has no per-region accounting, so every call the test makes to register a region, to allocate within it, and to have such an allocation refused beyond a limit cannot be satisfied. After the production fix the allocator recognizes dedicated regions, tracks how much each has used, refuses allocations that would exceed the reserved limit, and rejects registrations with a NULL name, zero size, or a duplicated name, so the zones test passes.
